claims.text: Wear resistance in high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by microstructural uniformity.
Controlled nano-CeO2 addition produces a homogeneous dispersion of hard phases through grain refinement.
A homogeneous hard-phase dispersion reduces localized stress concentrations and crack initiation.
FeCoNiCrMo0.2, FeCoNiCrMo0.2+WC, and FeCoNiCrMo0.2+WC+CeO2 coatings can be prepared on 316L stainless steel by laser cladding.
The FeCoNiCrMo0.2+32%WC baseline has an uneven distribution of hard-phase particles.
The uneven hard-phase distribution in the WC-containing baseline causes spatially unstable hardness and wear resistance.
Adding 2% nano-CeO2 to the HEA+WC coating is the controlled intervention.
Adding 2% nano-CeO2 refines the coating grain structure.
Nano-CeO2 produces a more uniform distribution of hard phases and minimizes local hardness variation.
Nano-CeO2 reduces porosity and crack sensitivity during solidification.
A homogeneous hardness distribution lowers friction variability.
A homogeneous hardness distribution minimizes wear-accelerating stress concentrations.
The nano-CeO2-modified coating will have a lower and less variable friction coefficient than the HEA+WC baseline.
The nano-CeO2-modified coating will have a more uniform hardness profile than the HEA+WC baseline.
The nano-CeO2-modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the HEA+WC baseline.
The proposed comparison holds laser-cladding parameters and 316L substrates constant between modified and baseline coatings.
The expected effect may be limited to HEA systems processed under rapid-cooling conditions similar to laser cladding.
The mechanism may not apply universally across other HEA compositions, processing conditions, or extreme wear environments.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in hardness uniformity, friction stability, and wear rate is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
